analyzed_vuln.description: In the #EXT-X-MEDIA NAME attribute handler, parse_attributes unconditionally evaluates gf_strdup(ret[i] + 5 + 1), assuming NAME= is followed by an opening quote. extract_attributes correctly allocates the token as its length plus one NUL byte; for the token "NAME=" this is a 6-byte buffer, so ret[i] + 6 is one byte past the allocation. strdup then scans from that out-of-bounds pointer, causing the heap-buffer-overflow read. The handler must validate the value/quotes and length before advancing, rather than blindly skipping a presumed quote (and blindly removing the final character).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A playlist accepted as M3U8 (beginning with #EXTM3U) must contain an #EXT-X-MEDIA directive with an empty NAME value, e.g. #EXT-X-MEDIA:NAME=. The line reaches gf_m3u8_parse_sub_playlist, extract_attributes produces the NUL-terminated 6-byte token "NAME=", and parse_attributes recognizes its NAME= prefix before passing the one-past-end pointer ret[i]+6 to gf_strdup. No TYPE or other attributes are needed because the overflow occurs while processing NAME, before later semantic validation rejects the incomplete media directive.
